title: Healthy Habits
description: Build healthy routines around sleep, nutrition, exercise and everyday well-being.

sections.title: Theory: What Makes a Habit Healthy?
sections.description: Learn the basics of healthy daily habits.

materials.content: Healthy habits are small actions that support physical and mental well-being. Regular sleep, balanced meals, hydration and movement can make a difference over time.

sections.title: Practice: Check Your Habits
sections.description: Identify everyday choices that support well-being.

exercises.prompt: Which habit can help you feel more rested?
exercises.hint: Think about consistency.
exercises.explanation: A regular sleep schedule helps support good sleep quality.

exercises.prompt: Drinking water regularly is part of maintaining healthy habits.
exercises.hint: Think about hydration.
exercises.explanation: Water supports normal body functions and hydration.

exercises.prompt: Which is an example of a healthy daily habit?
exercises.hint: Think about movement during the day.
exercises.explanation: Regular movement supports general health.

sections.title: Theory: Building a Balanced Plate
sections.description: Explore the role of variety and balance in everyday meals.

materials.content: A balanced diet includes a variety of foods. Fruits, vegetables, grains, protein sources and water can all contribute to a healthy eating pattern.

sections.title: Practice: Food Choices
sections.description: Practice identifying balanced food choices.

exercises.prompt: Eating a variety of foods can help provide different nutrients.
exercises.hint: Different foods contain different nutrients.
exercises.explanation: Variety can help people obtain a wider range of nutrients.

exercises.prompt: Name one type of food that can be part of a balanced meal.
exercises.hint: Think of a food group, such as fruit or vegetables.
exercises.explanation: Vegetables are one example; many other food groups can be part of a balanced meal.

exercises.prompt: Which choice adds vegetables to a meal?
exercises.hint: Choose the option made primarily from vegetables.
exercises.explanation: A side salad is a simple way to include vegetables.

sections.title: Theory: Why Sleep Matters
sections.description: Understand how sleep supports daily functioning.

materials.content: Sleep supports memory, attention, mood and physical recovery. A consistent routine and a calm sleeping environment can help improve sleep habits.

sections.title: Practice: Sleep Scenarios
sections.description: Apply sleep-hygiene principles to common situations.

exercises.prompt: Which is generally a helpful habit before bedtime?
exercises.hint: Choose the option that supports consistency and relaxation.
exercises.explanation: A consistent wind-down routine can help prepare the body for sleep.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence about sleep.
exercises.hint: Think about what the body needs after an active day.
exercises.explanation: Sleep is important for physical and mental recovery.
exercises.correctAnswer: A regular sleep schedule can support
phrases: A regular sleep schedule can support

exercises.prompt: Sleep can affect attention and memory.
exercises.hint: Think about how you feel after a poor night's sleep.
exercises.explanation: Sleep plays an important role in attention and memory.

sections.title: Theory: Habit Formation
sections.description: Explore how cues, repetition and realistic goals can support lasting habits.

materials.content: A habit often develops through repetition in a consistent context. Small goals, reminders and tracking can make a new behavior easier to maintain, although individual experiences vary.

sections.title: Practice: Design a Routine
sections.description: Apply habit-building ideas to a realistic scenario.

exercises.prompt: A person wants to walk more often. Name one practical strategy that could help them build the habit.
exercises.hint: Attach the new behavior to an existing routine.
exercises.explanation: A specific cue, such as walking after lunch, can make the behavior easier to repeat.

exercises.prompt: Upload an image that represents a healthy routine.
exercises.hint: Choose an image related to movement, sleep, food or relaxation.
exercises.explanation: This activity is reviewed as a practice submission.

exercises.prompt: Which strategy is most likely to make a new habit easier to repeat?
exercises.hint: Think about making the behavior predictable.
exercises.explanation: A consistent cue can help a behavior become part of a routine.
exercises.correctAnswer: Linking it to a consistent cue
options: Linking it to a consistent cue
Changing the plan every day without tracking

title: Green Living
description: Explore practical ways to reduce waste, save energy and live more sustainably.

sections.title: Theory: Understanding Waste
sections.description: Learn the difference between reducing, reusing and recycling.

materials.content: Reducing waste means using less, reusing means finding another use for an item, and recycling means processing materials so they can be made into new products. Local recycling rules vary.

sections.title: Practice: Sort the Choices
sections.description: Identify simple ways to reduce household waste.

exercises.prompt: Which action gives a reusable bottle another use?
exercises.hint: Choose the action that uses the bottle again.
exercises.explanation: Refilling a reusable bottle avoids needing a new single-use bottle.
options: Throwing it away after one use
Leaving it unused in a drawer

exercises.prompt: Recycling rules can differ between towns and cities.
exercises.hint: Think about local waste collection systems.
exercises.explanation: Accepted materials and sorting rules vary by location.

exercises.prompt: Reusing an item can help reduce waste.
exercises.hint: Consider whether the item is being used again.
exercises.explanation: Reusing an item can reduce the need to discard it and replace it.

sections.title: Theory: Everyday Energy Use
sections.description: Explore simple actions that can reduce unnecessary energy use.

materials.content: Turning off unused lights and electronics, choosing efficient appliances and adjusting heating responsibly can reduce energy consumption. The impact depends on the home and energy source.

sections.title: Practice: Energy-Saving Choices
sections.description: Choose practical ways to avoid wasting energy.

exercises.prompt: What is a sensible way to reduce electricity use when leaving a room?
exercises.hint: Focus on avoiding unnecessary use.
exercises.explanation: Turning off unnecessary lights reduces electricity use.
exercises.correctAnswer: Turn off lights that are not needed
options: Turn off lights that are not needed

exercises.prompt: Name one way to save energy at home.
exercises.hint: Think about lights, heating or electronics.
exercises.explanation: Turning off unnecessary lights is one possible answer.

exercises.prompt: Which action can help reduce unnecessary energy use?
exercises.hint: Choose the option that avoids energy waste.
exercises.explanation: Switching off devices when they are not needed can reduce energy consumption.
options: Opening windows while heating is on

sections.title: Theory: Choosing How to Travel
sections.description: Compare everyday transport options and their environmental impacts.

materials.content: Walking, cycling and public transport can have lower emissions per passenger than driving alone, depending on distance, occupancy and the energy used. Practicality and accessibility also matter.

sections.title: Practice: Travel Decisions
sections.description: Apply transport choices to everyday journeys.

exercises.prompt: For many urban trips, walking or cycling can avoid direct tailpipe emissions.
exercises.hint: Consider whether a vehicle engine is being used.
exercises.explanation: Walking and cycling do not produce direct tailpipe emissions.

exercises.prompt: For a short journey where it is practical and safe, which option avoids using a car?
exercises.hint: Choose an option that does not require a motor vehicle.
exercises.explanation: Walking avoids the use of a motor vehicle for that trip.

exercises.prompt: Name one alternative to driving alone for a short urban journey.
exercises.hint: Think of shared or active transport.
exercises.explanation: Public transport, walking and cycling are possible alternatives.

sections.title: Theory: Evidence and Green Claims
sections.description: Learn to assess environmental claims using evidence and context.

materials.content: Environmental claims should be evaluated by checking their scope, evidence, comparison baseline and life-cycle impacts. A product described as recyclable is not necessarily recycled in every local system.

sections.title: Practice: Assess a Claim
sections.description: Identify what evidence is needed to evaluate a sustainability claim.

exercises.prompt: What is most useful when evaluating a claim that a product is environmentally friendly?
exercises.hint: Look for verifiable information rather than appearance.
exercises.explanation: Clear scope and evidence help consumers assess environmental claims.
exercises.correctAnswer: Evidence describing the claim's scope and supporting data
options: Evidence describing the claim's scope and supporting data

exercises.prompt: A fair product comparison should use the same
exercises.hint: Think about the reference point used in a comparison.
exercises.explanation: Using a consistent baseline makes comparisons more meaningful.
phrases: A fair product comparison should use the same

exercises.prompt: A product labelled recyclable is guaranteed to be recycled everywhere.
exercises.hint: Consider local collection and processing facilities.
exercises.explanation: Recycling depends on local rules, collection and processing availability.

title: An Introduction to Mathematics
description: Learn mathematics progressively, from arithmetic and algebra to functions and calculus.

sections.title: Theory: Working with Numbers
sections.description: Review the four basic arithmetic operations.

materials.content: Arithmetic includes addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. These operations are the foundation for more advanced mathematics.

sections.title: Practice: Arithmetic Practice
sections.description: Practice basic calculations.

exercises.prompt: What is 12 multiplied by 8?
exercises.hint: Calculate 10 times 8, then add 2 times 8.

exercises.prompt: Complete the multiplication statement.
exercises.hint: Seven groups of six.

exercises.prompt: What is 9 × 7?
exercises.hint: Calculate 10 × 7 and subtract 7.

sections.title: Theory: Parts of a Whole
sections.description: Understand simple fractions and their decimal equivalents.

materials.content: A fraction represents part of a whole. For example, one half is written as 1/2 and is equal to 0.5.

sections.title: Practice: Fraction Practice
sections.description: Recognize equivalent representations of numbers.

exercises.prompt: Which decimal is equal to one half?
exercises.hint: One half is halfway between zero and one.

exercises.prompt: The fraction 2/4 is equivalent to 1/2.
exercises.hint: Simplify the numerator and denominator by the same factor.
exercises.explanation: Dividing both 2 and 4 by 2 gives 1/2.

exercises.prompt: Write one half as a decimal.
exercises.hint: It is halfway between zero and one.
exercises.explanation: One half is 0.5.

sections.title: Theory: Expressions and Variables
sections.description: Learn how variables represent unknown or changing values.

materials.content: A variable is a symbol that represents a number. In algebra, 2x means 2 multiplied by x, and an equation states that two expressions are equal.

sections.title: Practice: Algebra Basics
sections.description: Interpret expressions and simple equations.

exercises.prompt: The expression 2x means 2 multiplied by x.
exercises.hint: Juxtaposition of a number and variable means multiplication.
exercises.explanation: In algebra, 2x denotes 2 multiplied by x.

exercises.prompt: Solve for x: x + 5 = 12.
exercises.hint: Subtract 5 from both sides.

exercises.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to 3(x + 2)?
exercises.hint: Apply the distributive property.
exercises.explanation: Multiply both terms inside the parentheses by 3.

sections.title: Theory: Solving Equations
sections.description: Use inverse operations to solve simple equations.

materials.content: To solve an equation, perform the same operation on both sides to keep equality. Inverse operations can isolate the unknown variable.

sections.title: Practice: Solve for the Unknown
sections.description: Practice solving one-step and two-step equations.

exercises.prompt: Solve for x: 3x = 21.
exercises.hint: Divide both sides by 3.

exercises.prompt: If x − 4 = 9, what is x?
exercises.hint: Add 4 to both sides.

exercises.prompt: Adding the same number to both sides of an equation preserves equality.
exercises.hint: Both sides change by the same amount.
exercises.explanation: Performing the same addition on both sides preserves equality.

sections.title: Theory: Understanding Functions
sections.description: Evaluate functions and interpret input-output relationships.

materials.content: A function maps each input in its domain to exactly one output. To evaluate a function, substitute the input value into its expression.

sections.title: Practice: Evaluate a Function
sections.description: Calculate outputs from simple functions.

exercises.prompt: For f(x) = 2x + 1, calculate f(3).
exercises.hint: Replace x with 3.

exercises.prompt: If g(x) = x², what is g(4)?
exercises.hint: Square the input value.

exercises.prompt: A function assigns exactly one output to each input in its domain.
exercises.hint: Think about the definition of a function.
exercises.explanation: Each input must correspond to exactly one output.

sections.title: Theory: Angles and Trigonometric Ratios
sections.description: Review basic sine, cosine and tangent values.

materials.content: Trigonometric ratios relate angles to side lengths in right triangles. On the unit circle, sine and cosine correspond to the vertical and horizontal coordinates.

sections.title: Practice: Trigonometry Practice
sections.description: Apply basic trigonometric facts.

exercises.prompt: What is sin(90°)?
exercises.hint: Consider the top point of the unit circle.
exercises.explanation: The sine of 90 degrees is 1.

exercises.prompt: For an angle of 0°, cos(0°) equals 1.
exercises.hint: Consider the point at angle zero on the unit circle.
exercises.explanation: The cosine of 0 degrees is 1.

exercises.prompt: What is cos(0°)?
exercises.hint: At zero degrees, the unit-circle point is (1, 0).
exercises.explanation: The cosine of 0 degrees is 1.

sections.title: Theory: Understanding Limits
sections.description: Explore limits of simple functions.

materials.content: A limit describes the value a function approaches as its input approaches a particular point. For continuous functions, the limit can often be found by direct substitution.

sections.title: Practice: Calculate Limits
sections.description: Evaluate limits for simple continuous expressions.

exercises.prompt: What is the limit of x + 2 as x approaches 3?
exercises.hint: This function is continuous; substitute x = 3.
exercises.explanation: The limit is 3 + 2 = 5.

exercises.prompt: For a polynomial function, the limit at a point equals the function's value at that point.
exercises.hint: Polynomial functions are continuous everywhere.
exercises.explanation: Polynomials are continuous, so direct substitution gives the limit.

exercises.prompt: What is the limit of 2x as x approaches 4?
exercises.hint: Substitute 4 for x.
exercises.explanation: The limit is 2 × 4 = 8.

sections.title: Theory: Derivatives
sections.description: Learn the power rule for differentiating polynomial terms.

materials.content: A derivative describes the instantaneous rate of change of a function. The power rule states that the derivative of xⁿ is n·xⁿ⁻¹.

sections.title: Practice: Differentiate
sections.description: Apply the power rule to simple functions.

exercises.prompt: What is the derivative of x²?
exercises.hint: Bring the exponent down and reduce it by one.
exercises.explanation: The derivative of x² is 2x.

exercises.prompt: What is the derivative of 3x?
exercises.hint: The derivative of ax is a constant a.
exercises.explanation: The derivative of 3x is 3.

exercises.prompt: The derivative of a constant function is zero.
exercises.hint: A constant function does not change.
exercises.explanation: A constant has zero rate of change.

sections.title: Theory: Antiderivatives
sections.description: Connect integration with reversing differentiation.

materials.content: An indefinite integral represents a family of antiderivatives and includes a constant of integration, C. For example, an antiderivative of 2x is x² + C.

sections.title: Practice: Integration Practice
sections.description: Recognize simple antiderivatives.

exercises.prompt: Give an antiderivative of 2x.
exercises.hint: Reverse the power rule and include a constant.
exercises.explanation: The derivative of x² + C is 2x.

exercises.prompt: Which is an antiderivative of 3?
exercises.hint: Look for a function whose derivative is 3.
exercises.explanation: The derivative of 3x + C is 3.

exercises.prompt: An indefinite integral includes an arbitrary constant of integration.
exercises.hint: Different functions can have the same derivative.
exercises.explanation: Antiderivatives differ by a constant, represented by C.
